ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.3 et seq.; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.), s 233.3; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (limited partnerships); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 14.1 (individuals with significant control, applied by analogy to LP general partners); FINTRAC Guidance 5G, 6G, 8G; Hague Apostille Convention, Canada accession 12 January 2024, in force 11 May 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating corporate registry in the partner's home jurisdiction (e.g., HK Companies Registry, US Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; non-Hague origin states require dual consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada Consular Legalization Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and address proof of each individual partner with a 25% or greater interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Alberta Justice apostille for Canadian notarizations; Hague Apostille for foreign notarizations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT bank reference letter with KYC/PEP attestation from the funding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank maintaining the funding or letter-of-credit facility
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus certified English/French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of memorandum/articles of organization (MOA/AOA) of any corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating corporate registry or licensed filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO/control declaration and partnership agreement execution page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partners and 25%+ limited partners, notarized before a notary or commissioner of oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; no apostille required for Alberta-executed documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, Criminal Code (Canada) s 83.05 terrorist entity list, and SEMA/Magnitsky sanctions lists. Each partner must maintain a financial institution-grade KYC file including domestic and foreign PEP determination per PCMLTFA s 11.11 and FINTRAC Guidance 5G; records retained for 5 years after termination; any positive hit or declined business triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report under PCMLTFA s 7.1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, Government of Alberta (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), accessible at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; electronic filing is made through authorized registry agents using the RegistryX system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must contain the mandatory element 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 'SC' under Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, s 68(3). Only Latin-script (English/French) characters are accepted; non-Latin names, including Chinese characters, must be transliterated into Roman letters and, for French names, confirmed by a certified translator. Numerals are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may (i) obtain a fresh NUANS report and resubmit an alternative name; (ii) file a consent/waiver letter from the holder of any confusingly similar name; or (iii) deliver written representations to the Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the notice requesting reconsideration. A final adverse decision is appealable by judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for registry purposes: the LP must maintain a real physical address in Alberta capable of accepting service of process during normal business hours (Partnership Act, s 70), which may be supplied by a licensed registered agent offering virtual office services. However, for ISIC 4632 cold-chain meat and seafood importation, the bare virtual office is insufficient: the importer must hold a Safe Food for Canadians Act (SC 2012, c 24) licence naming a physical Canadian establishment and arrange a CBSA importer bond and cold-chain premises, which CFIA may verify at the listed address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (70-90%) for the first several cold-chain shipments, which are routinely referred to CFIA/CBSA documentary, identity, and physical inspection under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations; moderate (15-25%) risk of a registration-compliance verification visit to the registered office by Service Alberta or enforcement inquiry initiated from FINTRAC disclosures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3 (Alberta), ss. 61-78 (Limited Partnerships); Partnership Amendment Regulation; Safe Food for Canadians Act, SC 2012, c 24, ss. 21-35 (federal import licensing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Alberta Registry Services), Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form filed under the Partnership Act, Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta limited partnership; each limited partner must make a genuine capital contribution recorded in the Declaration of Limited Partnership to sustain limited-liability protection. Alberta law does not mandate an escrow account, but the lending bank will require traceable deposit of the subscribed contribution before activating Revolving LC and SWIFT TT facilities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the General Partner hereby subscribes the initial partnership units on behalf of the Limited Partner, and the capital contribution schedule set out in the Information Memorandum is approved. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Limited Partnership within the Province of Alberta, at the street address stated in the Declaration of Limited Partnership, is adopted for service of process with the nominated registered agent retained. FURTHER RESOLVED that the General Partner appoints a Compliance Officer, a Financial Controller, and an Import Trade Manager of the Limited Partnership, each authorized to execute banking instruments (Revolving LC and SWIFT TT), sign regulatory filings, hold CFIA import licences, and administer day-to-day operations. These resolutions are effective from adoption and remain in full force until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Banking Setup with Trade Finance Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian chartered bank corporate banking division or authorized foreign bank branch in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account in the LP's full registered name, complete KYC/AML clearance for all partners and beneficial owners, and request a revolving Letter of Credit facility with SWIFT TT origination. Deposit the paid-up capital contribution from traceable sources to satisfy bank onboarding requirements.
required_dossiers: Banking resolution of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's AML/KYC review is prolonged, submit an enhanced due diligence package (business plan, proforma invoices, supplier contracts) to the bank's compliance officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Food Safety and Import Licensing Division, Alberta Regional Office; co-regulators: Alberta Health Services (food premises) and Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Codes)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCR) Food Import Licence for frozen meat and fish importation, together with a municipal wholesale business licence and Alberta food premises/handling authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — Environmental Assessment and Regulatory Assurance Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Tier (activity-based) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA); a full EIA report is not required for a cold-chain wholesale warehouse unless hazardous refrigerant thresholds or significant wastewater discharge triggers are exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Refrigerant emissions (ammonia or halocarbon) must remain below the Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulations thresholds; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet Sewer Use Bylaw limits (pH 6-10, BOD/TSS standards); used compressor oils and contaminated cleaning materials must be managed as hazardous waste under the Waste Control Regulation (Alta Reg 192/1996); VOC emissions from cleaning and degreasing agents must not exceed National Ambient Air Quality Objectives thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code issued pursuant to the Safety Codes Act (RSA 2000, c S-1); structural load inspection certification for the refrigerated warehouse; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) registration with the Ministry of Labour and Immigration, including cold-storage hazard controls, worker safety program, emergency response plan, and workplace annual employer reporting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) via the Business Registration Online portal and GST/HST NETFILE
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership must obtain a Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 with the Canada Revenue Agency, either through the Business Registration Online portal or by mail, providing legal partnership name, registered office in Alberta or Canadian representative, foreign registration certificate, particulars of general partners, and indicating a request for a GST/HST account. CRA issues a 15-character BN/GST/HST registration number, which must be used on invoices and customs documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer a 'check-the-box' entity classification election. The limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax; the partnership itself is generally a registrant and collects GST/HST. Non-resident partners may elect under Canadian tax treaties or domestic rules to file returns on a net basis (e.g., section 216 election under the Income Tax Act for certain rental income) or elect to make a partnership GST/HST registration among qualifying partners. Hybrid mismatch rules in section 18.4 of the Income Tax Act apply to disallow excessive deductible expenses.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies (worldwide small supplier threshold) for non-resident businesses carrying on business in Canada; goods imported into Canada are subject to GST at border regardless of the threshold unless a section 168 import election or zero-rated schedule applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a government-run e-invoicing clearance mechanism; there is no statutory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping requirement. GST/HST invoices must include prescribed information (e.g., seller name, BN/GST/HST registration number, tax amount), and may be issued electronically provided the CRA is able to access and verify the records. CRA may require documented traceability in audits, but there is no API-based continuous transaction control system in effect.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including frozen beef, seafood, and meat products) are zero-rated supplies under Part V of Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act if the supplier is registered for GST/HST and the goods are exported in accordance with the conditions prescribed in sections 20 and 21 of the GST/HST Regulations. Zero-rating may also apply to basic groceries sold domestically for human consumption, but the export route requires proof that property was delivered outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13 Export Declaration or approved substitute)
Commercial invoice and foreign sale contract
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing export
Cargo control documents and customs coded destination (e.g., U.S./foreign port of discharge)
Proof of payment matching the exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipts evidencing receipt of foreign exchange proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits verify export evidence against customs records; failure to substantiate zero-rating results in reassessment at 5% GST/HST, interest, and penalties under sections 285 and 280 of the Excise Tax Act. Willful filing of false export claims may attract penalties equal to 100% of tax avoided or a fine of up to CAD 25,000, plus imprisonment for fraud. Refunds or input tax credits claimed on zero-rated exports are subject to recovery, with a limitation period generally of four years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; prudential regulation of banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); payment and settlement infrastructure is administered by Payments Canada under the Canadian Payments Act; Canada maintains no separate central foreign-exchange administration comparable to SAFE, and the Department of Finance Canada retains residual jurisdiction over the Exchange Control Act framework, which was repealed in 1952.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and maintains a market-determined floating exchange rate with full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There are no exchange controls, no FX transaction licensing, no prior-approval requirements for repatriation of profits or partnership capital, and no central-bank allocation of foreign currency. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely tradable on the spot and forward markets, and Canadian Schedule I banks may execute any lawful FX transaction without government authorization. The only practical hurdles are fiscal and reporting measures, not convertibility restrictions: (i) an Alberta Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, and Canada-source income must be reported to each partner via a T5013 statement; (ii) non-resident partners are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on Canadian-source business income and may be subject to Part XIII withholding or treaty-reduced rates on certain distributions, with the partnership responsible for remittances; (iii) the bank must file a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer report for every cross-border transfer of C$10,000 or more; and (iv) source-of-funds documentation is required for any inbound capital or outbound remittance that the bank's compliance desk considers unusual. None of these measures imposes a ceiling, an approval process, or a conversion mandate, and no hurdle prevents profit or capital repatriation once the tax returns and withholding obligations are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender regime and no mandatory conversion ratio. The Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and Canada's Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement prohibit any requirement to surrender foreign exchange or to convert export receipts into CAD within a prescribed timeline. The statutory remittance timeline is therefore immediate (zero days) and the mandatory conversion ratio is nil (0%). Exporters and importers may retain and deploy foreign-currency proceeds freely in Canadian or offshore accounts, provided the accounts are disclosed in tax filings and the funds are traceable under IFRS. For the import of frozen beef and pelagic fish, the CBSA applies the Bank of Canada daily noon exchange rate to convert foreign-currency invoices into CAD for Customs Act ad valorem duty valuation; this is a valuation rule, not a surrender or conversion obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (primary CAD clearing) + Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account + Trade Finance Desk (LC issuance and confirmation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined Canadian headline corporate rate (federal Part I 15.0% + Alberta provincial 8.0%). An Alberta Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level income tax; each corporate partner is taxed on its allocated share at the applicable federal and Alberta rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday for frozen beef/seafood importers. Alberta small-business rate of 2.0% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income is available only to a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner, not to the LP itself. Limited partners may deduct partnership losses only up to their at-risk amount (ITA s.96(2.2)-(2.5)). Manufacturing and processing deduction is repealed; import wholesale income is fully taxable.
